harper: FYI - we started seeing a p99 tail pop for long-context requests after onboarding kestrelx-extended-v1 for tenant acme-inc. Triggered ~Mar 16 2026 14:12 UTC. p95 went 140ms -> 380ms, p99 520ms -> ~2.1s on /v1/generate. No obvious 500s, just high tail latency.

harper: Repro + sample request below (small sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"kestrelx-extended-v1","input":"<~32k tokens sample>"}' \n  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
Request-id: rQ3-tnK-12e (from header).

devon: thanks, adding runtime traces now. Can you paste the exact model sha and the tokenizer bundle id used during the onboard?

harper: model sha: 9f3a2b7, tokenizer: kestrel-tokenizer-v2.1. We rolled the tokenizer simultaneously with the model because of unicode handling changes.

ingrid: quick hypothesis: tokenizer change increased tokenization density on CJK + long sequences -> more KV cache pressure and more attention work at late sequence positions. Can you share token counts distribution?

harper: minimal stats (aggregated): average tokens/request: 9.6k -> 12.1k after change, 95p tokens: 18k -> 26k. So yes token inflation on longer inputs.

sam: ops-bot alerted autoscaler churn in us-west-2 around the same time (horizontal scaling flapping). p99 latency coincides with scale events. Could be batching + longer sequences causing request queuing. :eyes:

ops-bot: [ALERT] autoscaler-flapping detected for pool:dedicated-gpu-usw2 at 2026-03-16T14:15:22Z. scale_up: 6->10, scale_down: 10->7 within 3m.

devon: can you enable detailed runtime debug for that tenant for a short window and include the following header so we get tokenization tracing: `X-Debug: tokenizer,kvcache,latency-trace`? I'll also dump kernel utilization and batch sizes.

harper: enabled for 10m starting 14:20 UTC. Attached excerpt of latency trace: average batch_size jumped from 8 -> 18 for long sequences, tail batches hitting sequence lengths ~28k causing >1s per token-window re-eval on current kernel path.

ingrid: mitigation ideas: 1) pin acme-inc to older tokenizer (kestrel-tokenizer-v2.0) as immediate rollback; 2) enable prefix-KV caching aggressively for streaming flows; 3) temporary request routing: route >16k token requests to a 'long-context' model variant (kestrelx-compact) that uses piecewise chunked decoding.

sam: operational mitigations we can do now: set max-inflight-per-worker lower to reduce queueing, force smaller batch cap for that pool, add a quick canary rollback to v2.0 tokenizer for acme-inc.

harper: doing the tokenizer pin rollback now for acme-inc (scoped flag). Monitoring. :thumbsup:

devon: follow-up: runtime team will investigate kernel slowpath for >16k sequences; suspected memory access pattern on the new attention kernels. Also need tokenizer team to run token density diffs across customer corpora before next rollout.

harper: after rollback p95/p99 dropped back to expected ranges within 6m (p95 ~150ms, p99 ~560ms). Keeping debug trace window open for 30m to gather more telemetry.

ingrid: opened postmortem backlog ticket to add automated token-density check to onboarding, and to document rollout playbook for simultaneous tokenizer+model changes.

sam: filing infra follow-up to tune autoscaler hysteresis and batch caps for long-seq pools.

harper: thanks all — will update thread with any new traces or customer impact notes. :eyes:
